rows.name: Merck & Co.
rows.thesis: A defensive large drugmaker with a 4.2% free-cash-flow yield and low 32% volatility, 3.9 points ahead of the ETF since purchase. The GAAP P/E of 145 includes the one-off charges in the filed figures; the cash flow is the better guide.
rows.risks: A pipeline setback or the later Keytruda patent cliff could weaken the earnings path.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 9.4% above), or a pipeline or patent setback breaks the earnings path.

rows.name: Targa Resources
rows.thesis: Fee-based gas gathering and processing that grows with Permian volumes. Its earnings depend on volumes, not oil prices, and volume guidance has not been cut, though the share has fallen in line with energy this month (-10%).
rows.risks: Middle East peace talks and lower oil could slow Permian drilling; it is only 4.6% above its 200-day average.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 4.6% above), or management cuts its volume guidance.

rows.name: Nucor
rows.thesis: The leading US steelmaker, protected by tariffs: 22% revenue growth, a P/E of 16.4 and a 4.6% free-cash-flow yield, 3.5 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Looser steel tariffs or weaker construction and industrial demand.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 10.9% above), or tariff policy on steel is loosened.

rows.name: DuPont
rows.thesis: The slimmer post-breakup DuPont is at its 52-week high, up 12% in a month while the index fell. It is 26 points ahead of the ETF since purchase and has a 3.8% free-cash-flow yield.
rows.risks: Only 3% revenue growth and a GAAP P/E of 77 leave little support if its momentum fades.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 12.1% above), or its lead over the S&P 500 ETF since purchase falls below +5 points.

rows.name: Hasbro
rows.thesis: Growing (+19% revenue) and profitable (18% margin), with an 8.0% free-cash-flow yield at a P/E of 16.2. It fell 3% in a week that favoured beaten-down tech, but it is still 15% above its 200-day average and my steadiest share (26% volatility).
rows.risks: Weak holiday toy demand or tariffs on imported toys.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 15.2% above), or Q4 results show the digital gaming segment slowing sharply.

rows.name: Viatris
rows.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt, with a 9.1% free-cash-flow yield. It is up 5% over a month in a falling market and 16 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Net debt of about half its market value and price pressure in generics.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 22.7% above), or debt reduction stalls.

rows.name: Target Corporation
rows.thesis: Q3 beat with raised full-year guidance. It is up 13% in a month, 2% under its high, at a P/E of 16 with a 5.3% free-cash-flow yield, and 2.7 points ahead of the ETF since purchase.
rows.risks: Weak holiday spending could undo the raised guidance.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 23.5% above), or holiday sales trends reverse the raised guidance.

rows.name: CrowdStrike
rows.thesis: Kept as an overreaction: Q3 (November 23) was strong (revenue +28%, record net new annual recurring revenue, guidance raised). The drop came from the all-stock Zscaler deal, not the business, and the share is still 20% above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Dilution and integration risk from the Zscaler deal, and 78% volatility.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or the Zscaler integration points to sharply slower recurring-revenue growth.

rows.name: Visa Inc.
rows.thesis: A payments network with 15% revenue growth and a 51% net margin, 1% under its high and 23% above its 200-day average. It is a steady share (28% volatility) that keeps my financials near the index weight.
rows.risks: Rules on interchange fees or a slowdown in consumer spending.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

rows.name: Omnicom Group
rows.thesis: Organic growth accelerated to 7.2% in Q3 as Interpublic synergies arrive. It has an 11.4% free-cash-flow yield and net cash, is at its 52-week high, and is my only communication-services name.
rows.risks: AI disrupting agency work, or setbacks in the Interpublic integration.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average (now 15.8% above), or organic growth falls back below 3%.

rows.name: NetApp
rows.thesis: Storage for AI data at a P/E of 24, with a 4.9% free-cash-flow yield and net cash. I'm holding it into Q2 results after the close on December 1, against guidance of $2.025-2.175 billion in revenue.
rows.risks: Storage peers fell 23-29% in a month, and a miss would hit a share with 69% volatility.
rows.exit_if: Q2 revenue or guidance disappoints, or it closes more than 3% under its 200-day average (now 9.0% above).

rows.name: Keysight Technologies
rows.thesis: A record fiscal Q4 on November 19 (revenue +41%, orders +53%) shows strong AI and networking test demand. The fall tracks the AI-hardware selloff, and it rose 6.7% this week.
rows.risks: With 75% volatility it would fall hard if the AI-hardware unwind resumes.
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 25% below its 200-day average (now 13.5% under), it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 20 points since purchase (now 11.4), or a fiscal 2027 outlook implies growth below 10%.

rows.name: Morgan Stanley
rows.thesis: Wealth-management fees and capital markets at a P/E of 13.6, with 16% revenue growth and a 25.5% margin. It is 0.9 points ahead of the ETF since purchase and has recovered from 14% to 12% under its 200-day average.
rows.risks: A deeper market fall would cut trading and deal fees.
rows.exit_if: It falls more than 15% below its 200-day average (now 12.2% below), or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 10 points since purchase.

rows.name: Illumina, Inc.
rows.thesis: Q3 beat with raised guidance, a 20% net margin and net cash; still 9% above its 200-day average, so the 29% monthly fall looks like the unwind of high-momentum shares, though I could not confirm a cause.
rows.risks: Revenue growth is only 5.8% at a P/E of 34.5, and an unexplained drop while health care rose could hide a company-specific problem.
rows.exit_if: It closes below its 200-day average, or it trails the S&P 500 ETF by more than 25 points since purchase (now 17).
